Let \(m=(p-1)/2=2t+1\), which is odd.

Suppose first that \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\). Then \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=p-1=2m\). Since \((a^m)^2\equiv1\pmod p\) but \(a^m\not\equiv1\pmod p\), we have \(a^m\equiv-1\pmod p\). Therefore
\[
(-a)^m=(-1)^m a^m\equiv(-1)(-1)\equiv1\pmod p.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)\mid m\). Conversely, if \((-a)^n\equiv1\pmod p\), then \(a^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\). Since \(a\) has order \(2m\), this gives \(2m\mid2n\), hence \(m\mid n\). Therefore \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m=(p-1)/2\).

Conversely, suppose \(b=-a\) has order \(m\) modulo \(p\). Let \(n\ge1\) satisfy \(a^n\equiv1\pmod p\). If \(n\) were odd, then
\[
b^n=(-a)^n\equiv-1\pmod p.
\]
Consequently \(b^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\), so \(m\mid2n\). Because \(m\) is odd, \(m\mid n\), which would imply \(b^n\equiv1\pmod p\), a contradiction. Hence \(n\) is even. Then \(b^n=(-a)^n\equiv a^n\equiv1\pmod p\), so \(m\mid n\). Since \(m\) is odd and \(n\) is even, \(2m\mid n\). Also \(a^{2m}=(-b)^{2m}=b^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p\). It follows that \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=2m=p-1\), so \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\).

Let \(m=(p-1)/2=2t+1\), which is odd.

Suppose first that \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\). Then \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=p-1=2m\). Since \(a^m\not\equiv1\pmod p\) but \((a^m)^2\equiv1\pmod p\), we have \(a^m\equiv-1\pmod p\). Hence
\[
(-a)^m=(-1)^m a^m\equiv(-1)(-1)\equiv1\pmod p.
\]
If \((-a)^n\equiv1\pmod p\), then \(a^{2n}=(-a)^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\). Therefore \(2m\mid2n\), so \(m\mid n\). Together with \((-a)^m\equiv1\), this proves \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m=(p-1)/2\).

Conversely, suppose \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=m\). Because \(m\) is odd,
\[
a^m=(-1)^m(-a)^m\equiv-1\pmod p,
\]
while \(a^{2m}\equiv1\pmod p\). If \(a^n\equiv1\pmod p\), then \((-a)^{2n}=a^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\), so \(m\mid2n\). Since \(m\) is odd, \(m\mid n\); write \(n=qm\). Then
\[
1\equiv a^n=(a^m)^q\equiv(-1)^q\pmod p.
\]
As \(p\) is odd, this forces \(q\) to be even. Thus \(2m\mid n\), and consequently \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=2m=p-1\). Therefore \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\).

Let \(q=(p-1)/2=2t+1\), which is odd.

Suppose first that \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\). Then \(\operatorname{ord}_p(a)=p-1=2q\), so \(a^q\not\equiv1\pmod p\). Since \((a^q)^2=a^{p-1}\equiv1\pmod p\), we have \(a^q\equiv-1\pmod p\). Therefore
\[
(-a)^q=(-1)^q a^q\equiv(-1)(-1)\equiv1\pmod p.
\]
If \((-a)^n\equiv1\pmod p\), then \(a^{2n}=(-a)^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\). Hence \(2q=\operatorname{ord}_p(a)\mid2n\), so \(q\mid n\). Thus \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=q=(p-1)/2\).

Conversely, suppose \(\operatorname{ord}_p(-a)=q\). Since \(q\) is odd,
\[
a^q=(-1)^q(-a)^q\equiv-1\pmod p,
\]
so \(a^q\not\equiv1\pmod p\), while \(a^{2q}\equiv1\pmod p\). If \(a^n\equiv1\pmod p\), then \((-a)^{2n}=a^{2n}\equiv1\pmod p\). Since \(-a\) has order \(q\), this implies \(q\mid2n\), and because \(q\) is odd, \(q\mid n\). The order of \(a\) therefore divides \(2q\), is divisible by \(q\), and is not \(q\); consequently it is \(2q=p-1\). Hence \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p\).

problem.theorem: Consider a prime $p$ of the form $4 t+3$. Show that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ iff $-a$ has order $(p-1) / 2$.
